limitations: Working tree changed concurrently during audit; initial vulnerabilities retained with original source evidence.
Independent baseline worker returned partial findings only due to usage limit.
No production penetration/load test or claim of complete safety.

findings.title: Anonymous callers can certify schedule changes as a head student
findings.summary: The public proposal and vote endpoints accept student identity and role from JSON. A caller can submit headstudent and obtain an officially_confirmed badge, or vary student_name to manufacture peer confirmations, without being a group member.
findings.remediation: Disable public social proposal, vote and listing endpoints until server-verified identities, group membership, role authorization and stable voter IDs exist. Disable sibling pseudo-RPC paths as well.

findings.title: Anonymous requests can run the administrator's schedule ingestion job
findings.summary: POST /api/v1/admin/sync-schedule has no authentication and directly starts a parser subprocess and PostgreSQL ingestion. Any reachable client can initiate repeated expensive refreshes and access internal job status.
findings.remediation: Require a server-only admin bearer token for both admin routes, compare it in constant time, reject by default if unset/short, and never put the token in frontend builds.

findings.title: Docker defaults expose database and cache outside the host
findings.summary: The supplied Compose deployment publishes PostgreSQL and Redis on every host interface. PostgreSQL has a fixed repository-defined password and Redis has no authentication configuration, allowing reachable clients to access the schedule stores directly.
findings.remediation: Remove database/cache host port publication, require a deployment-provided PostgreSQL password/DSN, bind backend port to loopback by default, and document TLS/reverse proxy requirements.

findings.title: Startup logs reveal database and cache credentials
findings.summary: Backend startup formats full configured DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL into log output. Credentials embedded in those URLs are disclosed to log readers who need not have database access.
findings.remediation: Remove full connection-string logging, avoid credential-bearing error propagation and report only configured/unconfigured state.

findings.title: Unbounded matchmaking lists amplify anonymous requests into database work
findings.summary: The public MatchWindows body accepts any length group_ids array and iterates it twice for database lookups without a body or group-count limit. Reachable anonymous callers can hold the shared database pool busy with repeated IDs.
findings.remediation: Disable the unfinished matchmaking endpoints; if restored, enforce bounded body size, maximum distinct group IDs, a request deadline and bounded aggregate queries.
